In Shanghai I saw Jimmie Pilcher-he is going to Peiping-
Dick Butrick- same old Dick- and Mr. Gauss.
The people I saw in
Shanghai seemed to think Gauss had not used good judgment, although
admitting he had a tough job. I wasn't there but I have been convin-
ced from the beginning he was not very cool. Evacuating all the women
and children down
the river on that tender in the face of a typhoon
which got so bad the Chinese quartermaster wanted to go back and the

be one of the greatest tragedies in American History. He looks

The next morning the Changsha steamed up the river to Chien-
kiang, about forty miles below lanking, and the Captain announced
he would be there for three days. I was headed for Hankow to join Bix
and all of our party were in a hurry, so we left the ship and tried
to get a car or bus to Nanking, but it was impossible. All public
vehicles apparently had been taken over by the army, but there was
a train that night at 6 P.M. so we got tickets on that. Our party was
now ten, four foreigners and six Chinese. We went to the station
about five thirty and found they were loading troops for the Front.
They were nice looking soldiers from Kwangtung, fairly well-eg nipped,
but very young looking. I ran over to a little shop and bought all
their cigarettes, 40 some packages, and gave then to the soldiers. Max
did the same thing at another shop and after that we really owned the
place. I never saw such appreciation. The officers thanked us many times.
police escorted us to a private room in the station where we could
sit down the whole station was jammed - served us tea, and when our
train was ready,
it was an hour late, they escorted us
through the gate
first, closed it behind us, and put us in the only first class compart-
ment on the train- we had second class tickets- before the gates were
opened to the rest of the passengers. It was really rather pathetic. We
had done nothing. It was natural that I should think of getting cigar-
ettes for soldiers moving up, but Max and I were the only ones who did
anything. The very

but they are the exceptions. They will never accomplish anything in war
until the leading classes really lead. No nation ever has. This war is
practically over for all real purposes. Do you remember Jack Jouett
